findings.title: Core state and feature adapters form a dependency cycle
findings.statement: The core state package imports a feature adapter that imports the core state package, preventing either boundary from being changed or tested independently.

severity.rationale: The cycle makes changes to shared state propagate across both packages and prevents isolated rollback.

confidence.basis: The repository dependency graph contains both directed edges at the reviewed revision.

findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The feature-specific adapter is treated as a dependency of the core state owner instead of an outer integration.

recommendation.action: Restore one-way dependency direction by placing the adapter behind a core-owned interface and keep feature code outside the core package.
alternatives: Extract the shared protocol into a dependency-neutral package when the interface is independently stable.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The package dependency graph contains no path from core-state to feature-adapter.
Core-state boundary tests run without loading feature-adapter.

verification_method.procedure: Generate the package graph at the candidate revision and assert the forbidden core-state to feature-adapter edge and cycle are absent.
Run core-state contract tests in an environment where feature-adapter cannot be resolved.

evidence.exact_observation: core-state -> feature-adapter and feature-adapter -> core-state are both present.
The isolated core-state test requires feature-adapter during module loading.
